description: Cooks every Sunday and keeps making dishes. Studies Japanese on their own, chose a Japanese history elective to understand the culture, watches anime and wants to visit Kyoto. Has three side projects.
tests: When one topic shows up repeatedly across different contexts (self-study, elective class, anime, travel), the topic-level generalization IS allowed. Guards against being so cautious that nothing is promoted
A clear self-statement ("I cook every Sunday... it's my reset") is promoted after one mention
Dishes are appended as separate records, not merged into one sentence
"Yesterday" in a message dated 9/13 is recorded as 9/12
Three projects mentioned once are grouped as records under one projects category; the robot arm's progress is appended

observations.note: Made shakshuka for breakfast with cumin and a bit of feta, describing it as easy.
Says they cook every Sunday, no matter what, as a reset for the week; chopping vegetables clears their head. They usually decide what to make that morning based on what is in the fridge.
observations.hook: Using the repetitive, hands-on activity of chopping vegetables as a way to reset and clear their head
observations.quote: It's my reset for the week, chopping vegetables just clears my head.

observations.note: Made shoyu ramen from scratch with chicken broth; making the broth took seven hours, and the tare was the hardest part.
observations.quote: Made ramen from scratch yesterday. Took me 7 hours for the broth lol

observations.note: Has been studying Japanese on Duolingo for about three months and chose to learn it without being asked.
observations.quote: Nobody asked me to learn it, I just wanted to.

observations.note: After about three months of Japanese study, read some of the soy sauce bottle label and felt proud of being able to do so.
observations.hook: Recognizing something learned in an everyday, real-world context
observations.caveat: Could read only some of the label.

observations.note: They chose a Japanese history elective to understand the culture behind food and language they are interested in, and asked beyond the syllabus how sakoku affected what people ate.
observations.hook: Understanding the cultural context behind food and language
observations.quote: I picked this elective because I wanted to understand the culture behind the food and the language I'm into.

observations.note: They found it funny that sushi was described as fast food in Edo-era Japan.
observations.hook: The unexpected contrast of a familiar food being historical fast food
observations.quote: Sushi as fast food is so funny.

observations.note: The student said they felt sad after finishing Frieren, but did not say what specifically drew them to it.
The student said temple scenes in anime always affect them strongly.
observations.quote: the temple scenes in anime always get me.

observations.note: The student really wants to visit Kyoto someday and is saving up, with next year as a possibility. They connected this goal to temple scenes in anime.
observations.caveat: Next year is only a possibility.
observations.quote: I really want to go to Kyoto someday… Saving up for it! Maybe next year.
